title: Tomato-Basil Chicken Cutlets with Whipped Ricotta
description: Thin chicken breast cutlets poach directly in a smooth tomato-basil sauce finished with whipped ricotta.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breast
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: plain smooth no-salt-added tomato passata
ingredients.note: Choose strained passata without pieces or added seasoning.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

ingredients.name: fresh basil
ingredients.note: Use a leafy sprig; keep whole for removal. Remove before serving.

steps.title: Even the cutlets
steps.text: Butterfly {chicken} into cutlets. Between two sheets of parchment, gently tap the thick ends with the flat face of a meat mallet to an even 3/8 inch.

steps.title: Infuse the sauce
steps.text: Simmer {tomato}, {broth}, {garlic} and {basil} in the HexClad over medium-low for 4 minutes with the lid on.

steps.title: Poach the cutlets
steps.text: Lower the cutlets into the sauce in a single layer and spoon sauce over them. Cover and cook gently for 5–10 minutes, turning once. Pull each cutlet when a sideways probe reads 165°F in its thickest center.

steps.title: Smooth the base
steps.text: Let the cutlets rest on a covered plate with a little sauce. Remove the basil sprig from the pan and bring the sauce to a full boil, then reduce to a simmer.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Whip the ricotta
steps.text: In a deep heatproof jug, blend {ricotta} with a ladle of the thickened sauce until completely smooth. Fold the mixture into the pan off heat.

steps.title: Dress the cutlets
steps.text: Slice the rested chicken across the grain. Spoon sauce beneath the slices and cover their cut faces with the remaining tomato-ricotta sauce.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups for two. Make ahead: Infuse the passata a day ahead and chill separately from the chicken. Add ricotta only at the finish. Option A uses tomato passata. For gentler Option B, replace it with an equal volume of plain, smooth butternut squash puree and loosen with broth as needed. For dairy-free sauce replace the ricotta with smooth silken tofu. Chill leftovers promptly in shallow portions and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the cutlets surrounded by tomato sauce for up to 2 months and whip in the ricotta after reheating for the best texture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in a HexClad skillet over medium-low, loosening with a splash of water if needed. Stir or turn the chicken gently, checking from 6 minutes, until it reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 266 kcal, 37.7 g protein, 13.5 g total carbohydrate, 6.3 g fat, 1.8 g fiber, 134 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
